agentClaim.summary: Recommend staying with reactive per-shape detectors, not generalizing: block-classify.ts's looksStructured() already composes independent boolean detectors (gutters, framing rules, box-char ratio, pipe tables, menu cursor, Q&A summary pairs) via OR, one detector per real Claude Code UI shape discovered in the field, each with its own test fixture from spec docs/specs/terminal-detail.md R21-R27's documented asymmetric bias (wrongly panning prose is free; wrongly wrapping structure is unrecoverable). This OR-composition is monotonic: adding a new detector can only turn more blocks into 'pan', never flip an existing 'pan' back to 'wrap', which structurally guarantees R25's safety bias forever with zero coordination between detector authors -- a property a generalized/weighted/statistical classifier would give up. Building a general layout-detection model now would be premature generalization: it adds tuning surface, breaks the monotonicity invariant, and the spec's own Open Gaps section already accepts real-miss-rate-unmeasured as a live known gap rather than something needing a new architecture. Concrete recommendation: (1) keep adding one small pure detector function per newly observed real-world shape, following the existing convention (regex/threshold constant + doc comment naming the false positive it avoids + the real capture that motivated it + a describe() block with the actual lines as fixture); (2) do not extract a DETECTORS[] array/registry until the flat early-return chain in looksStructured() exceeds ~10-12 checks -- currently 6, so YAGNI says leave it as literal if-returns; (3) treat each new bug report as exactly the same shape of PR the last two commits already were (menu-cursor fix, Q&A-summary-pairs fix) -- this is the intended steady-state, not technical debt to eventually replace.
evidence: web/src/block-classify.ts (read in full): looksStructured() is 6 independent detectors combined by early-return OR
web/test/block-classify.test.ts: one describe/it group per detector, each with a real-shape fixture and a comment naming the regression it guards
docs/specs/terminal-detail.md R21-R27: codifies the pan-by-default / wrap-must-prove-itself asymmetric bias as a business rule, not an implementation detail
docs/specs/terminal-detail.md Open Gaps: explicitly accepts unmeasured real miss-rate as a known, tracked gap rather than a defect requiring redesign
git log subjects (881fa33, 15b1203) show the last two changes were exactly this pattern: one new named UI shape, one new detector, one new test

recommendation.keep: flat OR-chain of small named pure detector functions in looksStructured(), one per real-world UI shape, each with its own regex/threshold constants and its own test fixture
recommendation.avoid: a generalized/weighted/statistical/ML layout classifier, or a plugin/registry abstraction introduced before the flat chain actually becomes unwieldy
recommendation.trigger_for_future_refactor: only mechanically extract to a DETECTORS: Array<(content: string[]) => boolean> + .some() once the chain exceeds roughly 10-12 checks; this is an extraction, not a redesign of detection logic
recommendation.key_invariant_to_preserve: OR-composition is monotonic -- new detectors can only add 'pan' verdicts, never remove one -- which is what makes R25's safety bias hold automatically as the file grows
